# Port progress

<!-- Generated by `npm run progress`. Statuses are preserved across regeneration —
     edit the status text on a line and re-run; do not hand-edit the structure. -->

Tracking the rewrite of 643 decompiled ActionScript 3 classes (`SWFimported/scripts`) into TypeScript/Phaser.

**21 / 557** game classes started · **13** verified · 5 marked not applicable · 81 third-party classes excluded.

```
█░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  3.8%
```

## How to use this file

Set a class to `ported` when its TypeScript equivalent exists, and `tested` when
its behaviour has been verified (a unit test, or confirmed in the running game).
Statuses are the four literals `not started`, `ported`, `tested` and
`not applicable`; anything else is reset on the next regeneration.

Use `not applicable` for classes that will deliberately never be ported — asset
stubs, dead code, third-party telemetry, or anything the engine already provides.
They are excluded from every total, so the percentages stay meaningful.

Append ` · wired` to a `ported`/`tested` line once the class actually does
its job in the running game — not merely when something imports it. A sweep
found 22 modules that were ported, tested and called by nothing, and wiring
the save layer then made most of them *reachable* while leaving them inert:
achievements are serialised but never evaluated, tutorial state is persisted
but no tutorial runs. Reachability is the floor, not the bar.

The flag is filled in as classes get wired, not backfilled, so its absence
means "not recorded yet" rather than "not wired".

Starting a fresh session? Read `README.md` first, then the "Core systems" section
below — everything else hangs off those.

## Skeleton work (not AS3 classes)

- [x] Vite + React + TypeScript scaffold, `strict: true`
- [x] Phaser 3 mounted in React, single instance under StrictMode
- [x] Asset sync from `SWFimported/` preserving SWF library IDs
- [x] React ↔ Phaser event bridge + Zustand store
- [x] Scale strategy (RESIZE, fixed 640-unit design width) + safe-area handling
- [x] Font loading and text-rendering policy
- [x] Preloader with a sample asset set
- [x] MP3 pipeline audit + runtime audio self-test
- [x] Placeholder gameplay scene with WASD movement
- [x] ESLint + Vitest + `dev`/`build`/`test` scripts

### Partially ported — blocked, not forgotten

- `SaveManager` — the **save-string half is complete**: storage layer, codec,
  slot container, the 63-field schema, and all 63 fields wired up. The `pw`
  key collision is fixed (`previousWorld` moved to `prw`).
  `save/saveSlot.ts` assembles a whole slot in schema order and reads it
  back — `encodeSaveSlot` / `decodeSaveSlot` are the equivalents of
  `updateSaveStringSlot` and `loadVarsFromSaveString`.
  Still to do: the local-SharedObject path (`initGame`, `loadGame`, the
  per-area `saveX()` writers) which stores fields individually rather than
  as a save string, and which needs the owning classes wired to their
  ported state. Server sync (`getServerSaveString`,
  `submitSaveSlotToServer`) is sponsor API and will not be ported.
  Server sync (`getServerSaveString`, `submitSaveSlotToServer`) is sponsor
  API and will not be ported.

- `ScreenAchievements` — the 36-achievement data table, the state model and
  `achievementCheck`/`updateAchievements` evaluation are ported and tested.
  The screen *rendering* (`placeAchievements`, `addText`) is not: it becomes
  a React screen. The value sources (`PartGameArea.temp*`,
  `ScreenUpgrades.tempWeaponsMaxed`, …) are injected, so they can be wired
  in as each owner is ported.

- `ScreenLevelSelect` — the progress table, difficulty cascade, current-level
  lookup and `getTotalValues` (which feeds the 15 NumberArray achievements)
  are ported and tested, along with its 4 save fields. The screen itself
  (world carousel, level buttons, tweens, particles) becomes a React screen
  and is not ported.

- `ScreenUpgrades` — the economy is ported and tested: 28 upgrade tables
  (1,173 balance values), level/price semantics, purchase, stat lookup and
  the maxed-weapon counts that feed the MaxedPrimary/MaxedSecondary
  achievements, plus its 4 save fields. The shop screen itself becomes a
  React screen and is not ported.

- `PartTutorial` — the 12-step queue state machine is ported and tested
  (unseen/queue/done lists, trigger conditions, the context-dependent steps
  that return to unseen between levels), plus its 4 save fields. Trigger
  conditions that read unported classes are injected via `TutorialContext`.
  The on-screen presentation (images, slide tweens, positions) is not ported.

- `ScreenEnemies` — the 20-entry bestiary and the `updateEnemies` discovery
  logic are ported and tested, plus its 1 save field. Note `knownEnemiesArray`
  stores *display* names ("Scared Ghost"), not ids, because the AS3 rewrites
  three of them to match the button labels. The enemies screen and the
  strength/weakness grid become React and are not ported.

- `Main` — status stays **not started**: the document class itself (screen
  routing, the display list, sponsor/API plumbing) is untouched. What exists
  is its 7 persisted flags in `onboarding/mainFlags.ts` — the six one-shot
  UI hints plus the one-time premium cash grant — with their save fields.

- `ScreenGame` — **all its data tables are extracted**; what remains is the
  level-running loop and screen plumbing, so the status stays
  **not started**. Done so far:
    - all three per-world arrays flattened into `levels/levelData.ts`:
      `levelDataModelW*`, `enemyModelW*` and `flagModelW*` — 405 levels with
      room size, mode, theme, PRNG seed, enemy composition and flag data
    - the 40 `enemy*Stats` tables in `enemies/enemyStatsData.ts`, with
      `enemies/enemyStats.ts` applying the difficulty and tier multipliers
      (the port of `PartGameArea.spawnEnemy`'s stat block)
    - the weapon loadout in `loadout/loadout.ts` with its 3 save fields
  Still untouched: the game loop, wave spawning, and the ~90 remaining
  statics that drive them.

- `PartGameArea` — **not started**, and mostly not separable. Ported so far:
    - `enemies/enemySpawn.ts` — the geometry tail of `spawnEnemy`
    - `enemies/enemySteering.ts` — turn-toward-target, accelerate, clamp,
      integrate (extracted from the behaviour loop, see below)
    - `waves/waveState.ts` — `spawnWarnings`' pacing and its
      draw-without-replacement pool, including the Flag/Boss balancing
    - `waves/spawnPlacement.ts` — off-camera search plus edge fallback
    - `waves/warnings.ts` — `handleWarnings`' countdown
    - `weapons/firing.ts` — `tankAttack`'s framework plus 4 of the 12
      primaries: **Cannon**, **MiniGun**, **Big Cannon** and
      **Gummy Bear Cannon**, covering three damage channels
      (Explosions, Bullets, Food) and both damage paths.
      The remaining 8 each carry their own mechanic and need dedicated
      sessions: Shotgun (deterministic fan), Flamethrower (lifetime +
      inherited velocity + loop sound), Laser Cannon (beam, own spread,
      owns the Laser channel), Magic Cannon (homing with a target
      budget), Timed Bomb Cannon (attaches and detonates on a timer),
      Poison Cannon (status effect), Cake Cannon (spawns secondary
      projectiles), Penetration Cannon (passes through, tracks hits).
      No secondaries are ported.
    - `weapons/bullets.ts` — straight-line flight and the hit test
    - `enemies/damageTypes.ts` — the strength/weakness system: 8 damage
      channels, per-type resistance tables, and the projectile -> channel
      map. Untyped rounds bypass it, as in the AS3.
    - `weapons/explosions.ts` — blast radius, flat (no-falloff) damage,
      multi-target hits and the one-frame `canDamage` window. **The
      Cannon is complete**: it explodes rather than dealing direct
      damage, so its damage runs through the `Explosions` channel.
    - `player/tankDamage.ts` — enemy contact damage, the Enemy Absorption
      upgrade, and boss knockback
  Together these close the core loop both ways: paced spawning of a
  level's real composition, a tank that drives and fires, enemies that
  die and pay out, and enemies that damage the tank on contact.
  **The enemy behaviour loop is 2,545 lines (PartGameArea.as:4499-7044)**
  and interleaves steering with damage, freezing, poison, burning,
  teleporting, healing, bullet collision, death, money drops and the
  strength/weakness system — it is not separable as a unit and none of it
  is ported. Damage types and explosions now *are* applied, so the
  remaining 8 primaries are no longer blocked on data — each still needs
  its own branch of `tankAttack` porting. Outstanding: homing, bullet
  reflection, penetration, the shield, status effects (fire, poison,
  freeze) and the Ice/Poison explosion variants that carry them,
  `DamageAddict` (healed by damage), boss knockback fed back into the
  tank's velocity, and defeat/victory handling.
